data.narrative:
Altara is an AI & Software company at an undisclosed stage, founded by Eva Tuecke and Catherine Yeo. The valuation landscape for this sector comprises one public comparable (Palantir, ticker PLTR) and eight private peers, including Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition. This peer universe reflects the fragmented maturity profile typical of frontier AI infrastructure.

Peer-median triangulation was not applicable to this analysis. A search across same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-valuation-tier filters within the AI & Software sector yielded fewer than three datapoints in each category, falling below the minimum threshold of three required for robust median estimation. While twelve same-sector peers exist in the broader AI & Software universe, none of the narrow stage and tier-specific filters produced sufficient coverage. Reliance on an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable selection bias given Altara's specialized positioning within frontier technology.

Without sufficient stage-aligned comparables or disclosed financial metrics from Altara, this analysis cannot triangulate to a defensible valuation range. The primary constraint is the absence of granular data on Altara's revenue, growth rate, or stage-specific positioning relative to the identified peer set. To advance valuation, either stage clarification paired with subset selection from the private peer pool, or disclosure of operational metrics (ARR, customer count, burn rate) would be required. The single public comparable provides limited precision without additional private market data calibration.
